chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili from al-Rifa'i, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who hired another man to dig a well for ten qamat (units of depth) for ten dirhams. He dug one qama, then became unable to continue. He said: 'Divide the ten dirhams into fifty-five parts. What one part amounts to is for the first qama, two parts for the second, and three parts for the third, according to this calculation up to the tenth.'

key_terms.خَمْسَةٍ وَخَمْسِينَ جُزْئًا: Fifty-five parts, the total sum of the fractional distribution
key_terms.قَامَة: A unit of depth or measure, here used for digging a well

ai.seo_question: How is payment calculated for a worker who completes only part of a contracted well-digging job?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of proportional compensation (*ajr al-mithl* or fixed wage adjustment) in labor contracts, specifically addressing the scenario where a worker completes only a portion of a defined task. The Imam’s instruction to divide the ten dirhams into 55 parts (the sum of integers 1 to 10) reflects a nuanced calculation where the worker receives a share corresponding to the specific unit of depth completed, ensuring fairness in partial performance of fixed-price contracts.
